exercises.name: Bench-supported one-arm row
exercises.main: Latissimus dorsi: draws the upper arm back toward the trunk.
exercises.secondary: Rhomboids and middle trapezius control the shoulder blade; rear deltoid and elbow flexors assist the pull.
exercises.base: Abdominals and spinal stabilizers resist rotation. Hips, thighs and ankle muscles steady both feet; the other arm supports the torso.
exercises.setup: Use a stable bench and a secure front rack anchor near the working hand's starting height. Clip one handle to one continuous pull line; keep the recoil path clear.
exercises.position: Plant both feet in a comfortable stagger. Support the opposite palm under its shoulder. Incline from the hips; keep neck and trunk aligned, knees soft.
exercises.move: Gently brace while breathing. Exhale and guide the working elbow toward the lower ribs; keep the shoulder away from the ear.
exercises.range: Stop before the torso twists, the shoulder rolls forward or the elbow has to travel far behind the body. Return slowly to a softly extended arm.
exercises.check: Both feet and the support hand stay planted. Shorten the pull or reduce resistance if you shrug, jerk or rotate.
exercises.easier: Rehearse unloaded, use less tension, or use a more upright supported row if the hinge is uncomfortable.
exercises.equipmentSystem: Individually selected long-line bands; KUZARO stock ceiling applies.
exercises.artCaption: START / softly extended arm                    FINISH / controlled pull

resistance.note: Record the chosen band rating and count for this exercise. No personal load is assigned.

exercises.name: Supported single-arm chest press
exercises.origin: Supported adaptation to complement the personal pull/triceps library
exercises.main: Pectoralis major: moves the upper arm forward and across the chest.
exercises.secondary: Triceps extend the elbow; anterior deltoid assists. Scapular muscles guide the shoulder blade.
exercises.base: Trunk muscles resist rotation; the chair and planted feet stabilize the pelvis and legs.
exercises.setup: Use a stable non-rolling chair and a secure anchor behind you near chest height. Keep the band beside the arm, away from the neck and face.
exercises.position: Sit tall with both feet planted. Start with the handle beside the chest, neutral wrist and elbow below shoulder height. Let the shoulder blade move naturally.
exercises.move: Breathe out and press forward smoothly while keeping ribs and pelvis steady. Do not lean or twist to finish.
exercises.range: Finish before the elbow locks; return only as far as the shoulder remains comfortable. Avoid a deep forced stretch behind the torso.
exercises.check: If the ribs flare, shoulder pinches or trunk turns, shorten the range and lower the load.
exercises.easier: Use an unloaded press rehearsal or a comfortable wall press-up instead.
exercises.equipmentSystem: Individually selected long-line bands; KUZARO stock ceiling applies.
exercises.artCaption: START / handle beside chest                    FINISH / controlled press
exercises.artReview: approved after correction: rear anchor, continuous band, closed clip and rear-facing handle frame; band length increases during press

resistance.note: Record the chosen band rating and count for this exercise. No personal load is assigned.

exercises.name: Seated straight-bar pressdown
exercises.secondary: Forearm muscles steady the grip and wrist; shoulder muscles hold the upper arms beside the torso.
exercises.base: Trunk muscles hold a quiet seated posture; both feet and the chair provide support.
exercises.setup: Use one secure high rack anchor, one rated pull line and a straight-bar attachment. Position a stable chair so the line stays in front of the body.
exercises.position: Plant both feet; sit tall. Keep upper arms beside the ribs and wrists in line with forearms. Choose a grip you can hold without strain.
exercises.move: Exhale and extend the elbows without pushing the shoulders down with body weight. Keep the upper arms nearly still.
exercises.range: Stop short of snapping the elbows straight. Return gradually into comfortable elbow flexion without letting the bar rise toward the face.
exercises.check: Avoid a rocking torso, bent wrists or moving the whole upper arm. Reduce load if the elbows or grip lose control.
exercises.easier: Rehearse the elbow motion unloaded or use a lighter single-handle variation matched to current tolerance.
exercises.equipmentSystem: Individually selected long-line bands; KUZARO stock ceiling applies.
exercises.artCaption: START / elbows bent                    FINISH / soft elbow extension
exercises.artReview: approved after reframing: complete high anchor and closed clip visible, bar centre attachment continuous, triceps focus and quiet seated base

resistance.note: Record the chosen band rating and count for this exercise. No personal load is assigned.

exercises.name: Short-arc shoulder raise
exercises.main: Middle deltoid contributes to lifting the arm out to the side.
exercises.secondary: Supraspinatus assists the lift; rotator-cuff and scapular muscles coordinate the shoulder.
exercises.base: Trunk muscles and planted feet keep the torso quiet; a chair supports the seated base.
exercises.setup: Begin without a band. Use a stable chair with room at both sides. This is a comfortable movement rehearsal, not a heavy raise.
exercises.position: Sit tall, feet planted, elbows softly bent and hands relaxed. Start with arms beside the body.
exercises.move: Lift in a slightly forward plane with thumbs comfortably forward or up. Breathe normally and keep the neck relaxed.
exercises.range: Use a small pain-free arc below shoulder height; stop sooner if the shoulder hikes, pinches or the torso leans.
exercises.check: Do not force the arms overhead or use a shrug to gain height. A smaller controlled arc is the aim.
exercises.easier: Move one arm at a time through a shorter comfortable arc, or omit if symptoms occur.
exercises.artCaption: START / arms lowered                    FINISH / short comfortable arc
exercises.artReview: Reviewed unloaded shallow sideways raise; middle deltoid red, shoulder-girdle assistant blue, quiet seated base; no front raise.

exercises.name: Seated brace with normal breathing
exercises.main: Abdominal wall: develops gentle trunk stiffness while breathing.
exercises.secondary: Deep spinal stabilizers cooperate with the abdominal wall; breathing muscles continue their normal work.
exercises.base: Chair contact and planted feet steady the pelvis. Hip and leg muscles provide light postural support.
exercises.setup: Use a stable chair. No band is required; this is a low-effort control drill.
exercises.position: Sit comfortably tall with ribs over pelvis and both feet on the floor. Keep shoulders relaxed and avoid arching the back.
exercises.move: Gently firm the midsection as if preparing for a light nudge. Take slow normal breaths without bearing down.
exercises.range: Hold only while breathing and posture stay easy. Release fully between attempts; no trunk movement is needed.
exercises.check: Do not suck the stomach in forcefully, brace maximally or hold the breath.
exercises.easier: Use a lighter contraction for fewer breaths with back support if comfortable.
exercises.artCaption: SETUP / balanced sitting                    HOLD / gentle brace and breathing
exercises.artReview: Reviewed quiet seated bracing and normal breathing; abdominal wall red, seated and foot base green; deep assistants described in text.

exercises.name: Supported sit-to-stand
exercises.main: Quadriceps and gluteus maximus raise the body from the chair.
exercises.secondary: Hamstrings and hip muscles coordinate the hip and knee movement.
exercises.base: Trunk and ankle muscles help balance the body over the feet; the chair marks the return position.
exercises.setup: Place a stable chair against a wall. Choose a seat height you can rise from without dropping or straining. Start without bands.
exercises.position: Sit near the front with feet about hip-width apart, heels planted and knees following the toes. Use armrests for assistance if needed.
exercises.move: Lean forward from the hips enough to bring weight over the feet, then stand smoothly. Breathe out during the effort.
exercises.range: Finish upright with soft knees. Bend hips and knees to return under control; touch down rather than falling into the chair.
exercises.check: Avoid knees collapsing inward, breath-holding or pushing through pain. Use a higher seat or hand assistance.
exercises.easier: Use a higher chair or more hand support; keep the same controlled return.
exercises.artCaption: START / seated support                    FINISH / controlled standing
exercises.artReview: Reviewed seated start and supported standing finish; feet planted; quadriceps red; ambiguous blue outer-thigh patch removed.

exercises.name: Seated single-leg band curl
exercises.main: Hamstrings bend the knee, drawing the heel back.
exercises.secondary: Gastrocnemius can assist knee flexion. Ankle-positioning muscles hold the foot position; hip muscles keep the thigh aligned.
exercises.base: Chair, opposite planted foot and trunk muscles steady the pelvis. The working thigh stays supported.
exercises.setup: Use a stable chair and a low anchor in front. Attach a manufacturer-approved ankle cuff to a light band, clear of chair legs and the other foot.
exercises.position: Sit tall with the working thigh supported. Start with that heel forward and the knee softly extended; keep the ankle comfortable.
exercises.move: Exhale and slide or draw the heel back by bending the knee. Keep the thigh and pelvis quiet rather than pulling with the hip.
exercises.range: Use only a comfortable arc with enough clearance under the chair. Return slowly; do not allow a sudden recoil or locked knee.
exercises.check: If the chair shifts, cuff slips, knee hurts or pelvis rocks, stop and reset; use less tension.
exercises.easier: Rehearse the heel slide without a band. Do not add resistance until the cuff and anchor are appropriate.
exercises.equipmentSystem: Individually selected long-line bands; KUZARO stock ceiling applies.
exercises.artCaption: START / heel forward                    FINISH / heel drawn back
exercises.artReview: approved after anchor correction: front low metal eye and closed clip visible, cuff above ankle, working thigh supported, band length increases; blue denotes local ankle control

resistance.note: Record the chosen band rating and count for this exercise. No personal load is assigned.

exercises.name: Supported calf raise
exercises.main: Gastrocnemius and soleus lift the heels.
exercises.secondary: Other lower-leg and foot muscles control ankle alignment.
exercises.base: Hip and trunk muscles keep the body upright; hands on a fixed support assist balance.
exercises.setup: Use a fixed counter or stable chair against a wall. Begin on a flat floor without extra resistance.
exercises.position: Stand with feet about hip-width apart, weight shared between them and knees soft. Hold support lightly but securely.
exercises.move: Rise slowly onto the forefeet while keeping pressure across the ball of each foot; breathe normally.
exercises.range: Lift only as high as you can stay balanced. Lower heels gently to the floor without bouncing.
exercises.check: Do not roll ankles outward, lean heavily forward or grip with the toes to force more height.
exercises.easier: Use a smaller lift or do seated heel raises if standing support is uncomfortable.
exercises.artCaption: START / heels down                    FINISH / controlled heel lift
exercises.artReview: Reviewed heels-down and gentle heels-up positions; calf muscle bellies red, Achilles tendons neutral; stable hand support.

exercises.name: Supported side leg lift
exercises.main: Gluteus medius and minimus lift the thigh away from the midline.
exercises.secondary: Tensor fasciae latae assists; other hip muscles coordinate the leg position.
exercises.base: The stance-side hip, trunk and ankle muscles steady the pelvis; hands assist balance on a fixed support.
exercises.setup: Start without a band beside a fixed counter or stable chair. Leave room to move one leg sideways.
exercises.position: Stand tall with the pelvis level and stance knee soft. Keep toes facing mostly forward.
exercises.move: Lift the free leg a short distance to the side while breathing normally, then lower with control.
exercises.range: Stop before the pelvis tilts, toes rotate upward or the trunk leans away. Keep the motion small and deliberate.
exercises.check: The movement comes from the hip, not a swinging leg or sideways bend of the waist.
exercises.easier: Use a smaller lift with more hand support; omit if the stance hip or knee is painful.
exercises.artCaption: START / steady stance                    FINISH / small side lift
exercises.artReview: approved as qualitative surface projection: working outer hip red, local hip assistant blue, stance side and trunk green; stable counter contacts, level pelvis, no bands

exercises.name: Supported shoulder-blade control
exercises.origin: Unloaded preparation for the personal pulling library
exercises.main: Middle trapezius and rhomboids gently retract the shoulder blades.
exercises.secondary: Posterior shoulder and rotator-cuff muscles help steady the arms while the shoulder blades move. Use a gentle movement, not a maximal squeeze.
exercises.base: Chair, feet and light trunk control maintain an upright seated position.
exercises.setup: Sit in a stable chair without a band. Rest hands comfortably on thighs.
exercises.position: Keep neck long, ribs settled and shoulders relaxed. Avoid starting in an exaggerated chest-out posture.
exercises.move: Gently guide the shoulder blades slightly toward one another, then release. Breathe throughout.
exercises.range: Use a small comfortable movement; stop before shrugging, arching or pressing shoulders forcefully down.
exercises.check: Do not pinch hard, pull the head backward or add load to compensate for poor control.
exercises.easier: Use a smaller motion or just practice relaxed posture and breathing.
exercises.artCaption: START / relaxed shoulders                    FINISH / gentle blade control
exercises.artReview: Reviewed gentle shoulder-blade motion; middle trapezius region red, rear shoulder assistants blue; neutral neck and seated base.

exercises.name: Seated neutral-grip curl
exercises.main: Brachialis, biceps brachii and brachioradialis bend the elbow.
exercises.secondary: Forearm muscles hold a neutral grip; shoulder muscles steady the upper arm.
exercises.base: Chair, feet and trunk control keep the pelvis and torso still.
exercises.setup: Use one light handle line from a secure low anchor in front, clear of the feet. A light handheld weight is an alternative.
exercises.position: Sit tall with both feet planted. Keep the working upper arm beside the body, thumb up and wrist straight.
exercises.move: Breathe out and bend the elbow without swinging the upper arm forward or leaning back.
exercises.range: Curl through a comfortable arc, then lower slowly to a softly extended elbow. Keep the band away from the face.
exercises.check: Avoid wrist bending, shoulder hiking or a tightening painful grip. Reduce resistance if control changes.
exercises.easier: Rehearse unloaded, use less resistance or choose a light weight you can grip comfortably.
exercises.equipmentSystem: Individually selected long-line bands; KUZARO stock ceiling applies.
exercises.artCaption: START / soft elbow extension                    FINISH / controlled curl
exercises.artReview: Reviewed same working arm in both panels, one handle and continuous low-anchor band; elbow flexion lengthens line; spare arm rests on thigh.

resistance.note: Record the chosen band rating and count for this exercise. No personal load is assigned.

exercises.name: Supported backward leg lift
exercises.main: Gluteus maximus moves the thigh backward.
exercises.base: Stance-leg hip and ankle muscles and trunk control keep the pelvis level; hands assist balance on a fixed support.
exercises.setup: Begin without bands, holding a fixed counter or stable chair against a wall.
exercises.position: Stand upright with feet under hips and knees soft. Keep ribs over the pelvis and toes facing forward.
exercises.move: Move one leg slightly backward from the hip while breathing normally, then return gently.
exercises.range: Stop before the lower back arches, pelvis tips forward or the body leans. A small arc is enough.
exercises.check: Do not lift higher by bending the spine or swinging the leg. Keep the stance foot planted.
exercises.easier: Use a smaller movement with more hand support, or omit if balance or symptoms limit control.
exercises.artCaption: START / steady stance                    FINISH / small backward lift
exercises.artReview: Reviewed small rearward leg motion with quiet pelvis and fixed hand supports; working glute red, posterior thigh blue; stance base green.

kuzaro.rule: One of each rating per kit; use one limb at a time where matching pairs are unavailable. Level limits are ceilings, not target loads.

hpygn.rule: Separate short-band/bar system; not interchangeable with KUZARO planner lines.

loadRule: Select resistance only after confirming comfortable motion, control, anchor/attachment ratings and current tolerance. Bodyweight or unloaded practice is valid. A 35 lb labelled band may already be too much. Label sums are not measured hand force or hardware ratings.
recoveryRule: Day 6 is easy skill practice, not a second hard full-body session. Rest instead if there is residual fatigue, pain or altered control. No schedule can guarantee injury prevention.

fullbody.equipmentNote: Placement describes the chapter. Each exercise retains its own equipment; HPYGN short bands are not automatically substituted for long-line movements.
